=====================================================================
CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
SUBJECT MATTER EXPERT INTERVIEW MEMORANDUM
=====================================================================
Matter No:         2024-AML-0876
Client:            Astoria Capital Partners LLC
Interview Type:    SME Witness Interview (Pre-Subpoena Prep)
Subject:           Suspicious Activity Review — Q3 2023 Wire Transfers
Date:              March 5, 2024
Time:              13:00 – 15:45 PST
Location:          Offices of Whitfield & Barnes LLP, San Francisco, CA
Interviewer:       Karen M. Whitfield, Esq. (Partner, Whitfield & Barnes)
Co-Interviewer:    Daniel Osei, CFE (Forensic Accountant, Kroll Associates)
Witness:           Angela Park-Reyes (Former AML Compliance Officer,
                   Astoria Capital Partners LLC)
Court Reporter:    Transcript prepared from audio recording
                   (Consent obtained; no stenographer present)
=====================================================================

PRIVILEGE NOTICE
---------------------------------------------------------------------
This memorandum is protected by attorney-client privilege and the
work product doctrine. Do not distribute outside the legal team
without express written consent from Karen M. Whitfield, Esq.
=====================================================================

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:00:18] KAREN M. WHITFIELD, ESQ.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Good afternoon, Ms. Park-Reyes. Thank you for coming in voluntarily.
Before we begin, I want to remind you that this interview is
protected under attorney-client privilege. Daniel Osei from Kroll
Associates is here as a consulting forensic accountant. Everything
you say today is confidential. Do you understand?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:00:52] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Yes, I understand. I want to be clear from the start: I raised
concerns internally about these transactions for six months before
I resigned. Nobody listened.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:01:20] DANIEL OSEI, CFE:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Ms. Park-Reyes, let's start with the timeline. When did you first
notice something unusual in the wire transfer activity?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:01:38] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
It was July 12, 2023. I was reviewing the daily SWIFT MT103
confirmations, which is standard procedure. I noticed a $4.2
million transfer from Astoria's operating account at First
Meridian Bank — that's account ending in 7741 — to an entity
called Verdant Holdings Ltd. in the Cayman Islands. The
beneficiary bank was Cayman National Bank, account ending
in 2298. I had never seen that counterparty before.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:02:45] DANIEL OSEI, CFE:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
What was the stated purpose of that wire?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:02:52] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
"Consulting services." No invoice number, no contract reference.
That's a red flag under our own internal policy — anything over
$100,000 requires supporting documentation. I flagged it in
our case management system, Actimize, the next morning.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:03:30] KAREN M. WHITFIELD, ESQ.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Who did you escalate it to?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:03:38] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
My direct supervisor, Marcus Delgado, the Chief Compliance
Officer. He told me it was a "legitimate vendor payment" and
to close the alert. I refused. He escalated it to the CFO,
Rebecca Lindstrom. Two days later, I was told the matter had
been "resolved at the executive level" and I should focus on
other priorities.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:04:45] DANIEL OSEI, CFE:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Did you document that conversation?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:04:52] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
I did. I kept contemporaneous notes in a personal notebook, and
I emailed myself a summary from my personal Gmail account to
create a timestamp. I know that was against company policy, but
I was worried.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:05:22] KAREN M. WHITFIELD, ESQ.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
We'll come back to those notes. Let's talk about the pattern.
How many transactions are we talking about?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:05:38] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Between July 12 and September 28, 2023, I identified 23
outbound wires to Verdant Holdings. Total value was
approximately $47.8 million. They all went through the same
correspondent bank — Citibank New York, SWIFT code CITIUS33.
Each wire was just under $5 million, which I believe was
deliberate structuring to avoid enhanced due diligence
thresholds.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:07:02] DANIEL OSEI, CFE:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Were there any other counterparties involved?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:07:10] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Yes. Beginning in August, I started seeing transfers to two
other entities: Northgate Advisory SA in Geneva, and a
Delaware-registered shell called Blue Harbor Consulting Inc.
I later learned that Blue Harbor's registered agent was the
same law firm that handled Astoria's 2021 restructuring —
Sterling & Vance LLP in Wilmington.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:08:30] KAREN M. WHITFIELD, ESQ.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Did you file a Suspicious Activity Report with FinCEN?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:08:40] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
I prepared a draft SAR on August 3, 2023. I was instructed by
Marcus Delgado not to file it. He said the firm's outside
counsel — that would be your firm, Ms. Whitfield — had advised
that the transactions were "within normal business parameters."
I disagreed, but I was overruled.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:09:45] KAREN M. WHITFIELD, ESQ.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
I want to be careful here. I can't confirm or deny what advice
was given, but I can tell you that no partner at this firm
authorized any communication suggesting these transactions
were legitimate. Do you have the draft SAR?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:10:20] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
I have a copy. It's on an encrypted USB drive that I gave to
my attorney, Patricia Nakamura at Nakamura & Holt. She has it
in a safety deposit box at Wells Fargo on Montgomery Street.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:11:00] DANIEL OSEI, CFE:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Let's shift to the individuals involved. Who at Astoria had
signing authority on the operating account?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:11:15] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Three people: Marcus Delgado, Rebecca Lindstrom, and a
senior vice president named Geoffrey Tanaka. Tanaka left the
firm abruptly in October 2023 — right after I resigned. I
believe he relocated to Singapore.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:12:20] KAREN M. WHITFIELD, ESQ.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Did you ever meet Geoffrey Tanaka in person?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:12:28] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Twice. Once at the 2022 holiday party at the St. Regis,
and once at a board retreat in Napa. He was close with
Rebecca Lindstrom. I always suspected they had a personal
relationship outside of work, but I never had proof.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:13:30] DANIEL OSEI, CFE:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Let's talk about the offshore structure. Did you ever see
any documentation about Verdant Holdings?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:13:42] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Only what was in the wire instructions. The beneficiary
address was listed as "P.O. Box 31489, Grand Cayman,
KY1-1206, Cayman Islands." The directors were listed as
two nominees — a Cypriot national named Stavros
Georgiou and a British Virgin Islands company called
Meridian Trust Services Ltd. I ran a World-Check
screening and found that Stavros Georgiou was also a
director of a company that had been sanctioned by OFAC
in 2019 — Palladium Energy Group.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:15:20] KAREN M. WHITFIELD, ESQ.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Did you report that OFAC nexus internally?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:15:28] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
I did. I sent an email to Marcus Delgado and Rebecca
Lindstrom on August 14, 2023, marked "URGENT — Potential
OFAC Exposure." I never received a response. Three weeks
later, I was placed on a performance improvement plan for
"insufficient attention to detail."

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:16:30] DANIEL OSEI, CFE:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Did anyone else on the compliance team share your concerns?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:16:40] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
One person. A junior analyst named Priya Deshpande. She
helped me compile the transaction data. She was terminated
in November 2023 for "restructuring reasons." I believe
she was retaliated against.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:17:35] KAREN M. WHITFIELD, ESQ.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Let's discuss the regulatory framework. What obligations
did Astoria have under the Bank Secrecy Act?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:17:48] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
As a registered investment adviser with over $100 million
in assets under management, we were required to maintain
an AML program under the USA PATRIOT Act Section 326.
We also had obligations under FinCEN's 2020 AML
effectiveness rules. Our last independent test was
conducted by KPMG in 2021, and it identified several
deficiencies that were never remediated.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:19:20] DANIEL OSEI, CFE:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
What deficiencies?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:19:28] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Three major ones. First, we had no automated screening
for correspondent banking relationships. Second, our
transaction monitoring thresholds hadn't been updated
since 2018. Third, we had no formal training program for
the compliance team — which is ironic, because I was the
one who was told I needed "more training."

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:20:45] KAREN M. WHITFIELD, ESQ.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Ms. Park-Reyes, I want to thank you for your candor. I
have one final question. If this matter proceeds to
litigation or a regulatory enforcement action, are you
willing to testify?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:21:10] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
I am. I have nothing to hide. I did my job. The people
who didn't do theirs are the ones who should be worried.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:21:35] KAREN M. WHITFIELD, ESQ.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Thank you. Daniel, do you have any final questions?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:21:42] DANIEL OSEI, CFE:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Just one. Ms. Park-Reyes, do you still have access to
your Astoria email account?

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:21:50] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
No. They disabled it the day I resigned. But I exported
my entire mailbox to a PST file before I left, and I
gave a copy to Patricia Nakamura. It contains
approximately 14,000 emails, including all the
escalations I sent.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:22:30] KAREN M. WHITFIELD, ESQ.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
That's very helpful. This concludes the interview.
The recording will be transcribed and provided to
you for review within 14 days. If you need to reach
me, please contact my paralegal, Sandra Whitcombe,
at the number on your copy of the engagement letter.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:23:00] ANGELA PARK-REYES:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Thank you, Ms. Whitfield. Thank you, Mr. Osei.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
[13:23:08] END OF INTERVIEW
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Recording stopped at 15:45 PST.
